title: What If the Roman Empire Never Fell?

segments.narration: In 476, Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, the last emperor in the West. Historians call it the end of the Western Empire. But what if Rome never fell?
segments.visual_description: Approximate 3D reconstruction of a generic late Roman city at dusk; slow crane down over the forum.
segments.camera_direction: crane down from high over the city walls to the forum
segments.animation_instructions: Badge: APPROXIMATE RECONSTRUCTION. No text in 3D.

segments.narration: Under Trajan, around 117, Rome ruled the whole Mediterranean, from Britain to Mesopotamia.
segments.visual_description: Map of the empire c. 117 CE (AWMC extent) filling in over the Mediterranean.

segments.narration: In 395, Theodosius the First died. His sons ruled East and West, and no one ruled both halves again.
segments.visual_description: Map: the empire splits into western (red) and eastern (blue) halves.
segments.animation_instructions: West and East fade in one after the other with region labels.

segments.narration: Visigoths sacked Rome in 410. Vandals took Carthage, the West's grain port, in 439, then sacked Rome in 455.
By the 480s, the West was a patchwork of kingdoms. The East, ruled from Constantinople, lasted until 1453.
segments.visual_description: Map: the western half fades away; successor peoples labelled at approximate locations; the East remains.
segments.camera_direction: pull back to the whole Mediterranean
segments.animation_instructions: No successor-kingdom borders are drawn (no openly licensed data); labels only.

segments.narration: Historians even debate the ending: some prefer 480, others say Rome transformed rather than fell.
segments.visual_description: Comparison card: decline and fall versus transformation.

segments.narration: Now, the alternate history. Suppose Carthage holds in 439. The West keeps Africa's grain and taxes, and Odoacer never takes Italy.
segments.visual_description: Hypothetical map: the western empire hatched in purple; grain route Carthage to Rome draws across the sea.
segments.camera_direction: push in on the western Mediterranean
segments.animation_instructions: Dip to black into this scene; ALTERNATE HISTORY badge.

segments.narration: In this scenario, Roman engineering keeps building: water mills like Barbegal's spread to many cities, and great domes like Hagia Sophia's rise in the West.
segments.visual_description: Hypothetical 3D Roman city in 1000 CE: aqueduct, water mills, domed basilica, harbor; flyover.
segments.camera_direction: flyover along the aqueduct toward the domed basilica

segments.narration: This is one possibility, not a prediction. A surviving Rome might still have split apart, or transformed.
